claims: U.S. consumer prices rose 0.9% in March 2026.
Annual CPI (Headline) was 3.3% in March 2026.
3.3% annual inflation rate is the highest since May 2024.
Gasoline prices recorded a 21.2% monthly jump in March 2026.
Gasoline monthly jump was the largest since data collection began in 1967.
Gasoline prices contributed nearly 75% of the total monthly CPI rise in March 2026.
Core CPI rose 0.2% monthly in March 2026.
Core CPI rose 2.6% year-over-year in March 2026.
Energy prices rose 10.9% monthly in March 2026.
Energy makes up roughly 7% of the CPI basket.
Energy's overall economic impact is closer to 15% due to its influence on other goods.
Consumer sentiment reached the lowest level in the history of the University of Michigan survey.
CPI for April 2026 is scheduled to be released on May 12, 2026.
Several CPI series are being rebased to December 2024=100.
CPI is calculated by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS).
CPI measures the average change over time in prices paid by consumers for a market basket of goods and services.
Percentage change in the CPI from one period to another represents the inflation rate.
CPI-U is Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers.
CPI-U is the most common type of CPI.
CPI-W is Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers.
CPI-W is used to calculate the cost-of-living adjustments (COLAs) for Social Security recipients.
